message.content:
In most mammalian cells you’ll find somewhere between **hundreds and thousands** of mitochondria—typically around **1 000–5 000** per cell, depending on cell type, metabolic demand, and developmental stage. For example:

| Cell type | Typical mitochondrial count |
|-----------|-----------------------------|
| Neurons (high energy demand) | ~10 000–20 000 |
| Hepatocytes (metabolic hub) | ~2 000–8 000 |
| Muscle fibers (especially cardiac) | ~5 000–15 000 |
| Erythrocytes (no mitochondria after maturation) | 0 |

These figures are averages; actual counts can vary widely within tissues and under different physiological conditions.
